transcript.content: Hi, it's good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Uh, yeah—so I came in because I just feel really restless, like I’m crawling out of my skin when I’m supposed to sit still. Like in the radiology suite, or even in class, I’ll be trying to just stay put and listen, but I end up shifting around, pacing if I can, or making up some reason to go move.

I kept thinking I could just tough it out, you know, like everybody gets antsy sometimes, but it’s been months and it’s still happening. It’s weird because the rooms are already kind of busy, with machines and people coming in and out, and I’ll be thinking about that too, but the main thing is I just can’t seem to sit still when I’m supposed to.
Did this restless feeling start after you began or changed any medication?

I don’t really know. I mean, I’m not sure I’d connect it to a medication change or anything like that. I’ve been trying to think back, but it all kind of blurs together—like school stuff, the hospital environment, everything’s always moving—and I don’t have a clear “oh, it started right after that” moment.
Have you had a period where you felt unusually energized or high compared with your normal self?

I’m not really sure what would count as “unusually high.” Like, I get keyed up sometimes, but it’s hard to tell if that’s me being energized or just, you know, the day being hectic. In radiology there’s always someone calling for something or a machine beeping, and then I’ll get home and still feel kind of wound up, but I don’t know if I’d call it high compared to normal.

Sorry, I’m kind of going off—short answer is I haven’t really noticed a clear period like that.
Do you ever feel an urge to pull out your hair?

Um… pull out my hair? I don’t think so. Like, I mess with my hair sometimes if I’m just sitting there, but I don’t really have this urge to pull it out or anything.

I mean, sometimes my hands are just doing something before I even notice, like tapping or fidgeting, and then I realize I’ve been messing with the edge of my sleeve or whatever—but hair pulling, no, not that I’ve noticed.
When you’re sitting still, do you feel an inner urge to move?

Yeah—definitely. That’s honestly kind of why I came in. If I’m supposed to just sit still, like in class or in the radiology suite when there’s a pause, it feels like I’m crawling out of my skin.

I’ll try to tough it out, like just tell myself to sit there, but then I’m shifting around, bouncing my leg, getting up to pace, or finding some reason to go check something even if I probably don’t need to. It’s been going on for months, and I keep thinking I should be able to just sit like everyone else, but I can’t really.
Did you have this same kind of trouble sitting still when you were a child?

Yeah, I think so. My parents actually still bring up those elementary school conferences—like the teachers would say I was always getting out of my seat, calling out, or starting stuff before they’d even finished giving directions.

I mean, they kind of tell it like it’s funny now, but at the time I guess it was a whole thing. And that was definitely way before middle school, not just something that started with radiology training or all the stress now.
As a child, did you often have trouble paying attention or finishing schoolwork?

Honestly, I’m not totally sure. I remember the sitting-still stuff way more clearly because people talked about that a lot.

With schoolwork… I mean, I did homework, but I don’t remember if it was like a consistent “couldn’t finish” thing or just normal kid stuff. My memory of elementary school is kind of patchy—like I remember random things, the classroom layout, this one pencil sharpener that everyone fought over—but not really whether I was regularly struggling to pay attention or finish assignments.
As a child, did you often lose things like schoolwork, pencils, or books?

I’m not really sure. I don’t have a clear memory of that specifically—like losing pencils or books or turning in crumpled worksheets or whatever.

I remember having a backpack that was kind of a disaster, but I feel like every kid’s backpack was gross at some point, you know? Mine had old snack wrappers and broken crayons—actually I remember this one time a juice box leaked and everything smelled awful for like a week—but I don’t know if that means I was constantly losing school stuff.

So… maybe? But I can’t honestly say I remember it being a regular problem.
Do you often have trouble paying attention when people are speaking to you?

Um… I don’t know, maybe? Like, I can usually hear people talking, but sometimes I realize halfway through that I’m thinking about something else, or I’m waiting for my turn to say something and then I’m not totally sure what they just said.

Actually, that happens more when someone is explaining something kind of long. Like if they’re giving a whole story with extra details, I’ll start thinking about one random part of it—like if they mention their car, then I’m thinking about my car making a weird sound last week, and then suddenly they’re still talking and I’m like, wait, where are we?

So… yeah, I guess it can happen, but I’m not sure how often is “often,” if that makes sense.
When you get up and move around, does that restless feeling ease up?

Yeah, usually. Like, once I actually get up and move, it takes the edge off a little. Not like it totally goes away, but it’s better than just sitting there feeling like I’m about to jump out of my chair.

That’s kind of why I came in, honestly. In the radiology suite or in class, when I’m supposed to just stay still and focus, I get this crawling-out-of-my-skin feeling. I’ll start shifting around, or pacing if I can, or I’ll make up some reason to go do something—check on something, grab something, whatever. I kept thinking I could just tough it out, but it’s been months and I still end up needing to move.
When you feel restless, are you also feeling worried or anxious?

I’m not totally sure. I mean, sometimes I’m annoyed by it, like frustrated that I can’t just sit still like everyone else seems to, but I don’t know if I’d call it worried.

Like, if I’m sitting there and I feel restless, my brain kind of starts looking for something else to do—actually, that makes me think of when you’re in a waiting room and the TV is on some random cooking show and you’re not watching it but somehow you know everything they’re making… sorry, that’s not really what you asked.

I guess… I haven’t really noticed it as anxiety. It feels more like I just need to move, but I don’t know. Maybe sometimes there’s worry mixed in? I’d have to pay more attention to it.
Are you taking, or have you recently taken, any antipsychotic or nausea medicines such as aripiprazole, risperidone, quetiapine, haloperidol, metoclopramide, or prochlorperazine?

Um… I don’t think so? Those names sound kind of familiar, but mostly from, like, hearing them in the hospital or seeing stuff in charts, not from me taking them.

I don’t take anything like that that I know of. I mean, I’ve taken regular stuff before, like if I felt sick or whatever, but I’m not sure about those specific nausea ones. Meto—metoclopramide? I don’t think I’ve had that. Prochlor… yeah, I don’t think so.

Sorry, I’m trying to remember if they ever gave me something for nausea, but nothing is jumping out. So I’d say no, not recently, at least not that I know of.
Do you spend a lot of time worrying about different things?

I don’t know if I’d say a lot. I mean, I worry about normal stuff, I guess—like school, work, whether I forgot something—but then sometimes I’ll start thinking about one thing and it turns into, like, five other things.

But I’m not sure it’s “worrying” exactly. Sometimes my mind just jumps around. Like I’ll be thinking about an assignment, then remember I need to text someone back, then suddenly I’m thinking about whether I left my laundry in the washer. Sorry, that’s probably not what you mean.

So… maybe some, but I haven’t really noticed it as me sitting around worrying all the time.
Do you find it hard to control your worrying once it starts?

I’m not totally sure. If I’m actually worried about something, sometimes it kind of keeps popping back up, but I don’t know if that’s me not being able to control it or just my brain bouncing around.

Like I’ll try to move on and then I’m suddenly thinking about it again because something reminded me—kind of like when you’re trying not to think about a song and then it’s stuck in your head all day. Sorry, that’s a weird comparison.

So… I guess maybe sometimes it’s hard, but I haven’t really paid attention to whether I can “control” it. It doesn’t feel like I’m sitting there choosing to worry, if that makes sense.
Do you often have trouble keeping track of tasks or appointments in your daily life?

Yeah… I mean, maybe? I’m trying to think of what counts as “trouble keeping track.” Like I use my phone calendar sometimes, and if something is written down I’m usually okay, but then I’ll put reminders in weird places and forget I even made the reminder.

Appointments are kind of different because, like, if it’s important I’ll be thinking about it a bunch beforehand, but then also I’ve definitely had times where I’m like, “Oh, that was today?” Or I’ll remember the day but not the time, which is annoying.

Tasks… I don’t know, daily life stuff kind of piles up. But I don’t want to make it sound dramatic. I just feel like I’m always trying to keep a mental list, and then something else happens and the list disappears. Sorry, I’m rambling. So… yes, I guess I do have some trouble with that.
Do you often put off tasks that require sustained mental effort, like paperwork, studying, or long reading assignments?

Um… yeah, I’m not totally sure how to answer that. I mean, I definitely don’t jump excitedly into stuff like paperwork or reading something long, but I don’t know if I “often put it off” in the way you mean.

Like, if I have to read something for class, I’ll tell myself I’m going to start after I get water or check one thing, and then somehow I’m reorganizing my desk or watching some random video about, like, how airport scanners work—which is kind of related to radiology, I guess, but not actually the assignment.

Sorry, I’m getting off track. So… I guess I do put off that kind of stuff sometimes, especially if it feels like it’s going to take a lot of sitting still and focusing, but I haven’t really kept track of how much.
Do you often feel physically tense, like your muscles are tight?

I’m not really sure. I don’t usually think about my muscles being tight unless someone points it out, like if I’m sitting weird or I’ve been at a computer too long.

I mean, sometimes my shoulders feel kind of up by my ears, but I don’t know if that’s tension or just posture, because in the radiology lab we’re always leaning over stuff and then I realize I’ve been standing awkwardly for like twenty minutes. Or maybe that’s not what you mean.

So… I haven’t really noticed feeling physically tense all the time, no.
Are you currently taking a stimulant medicine for attention, such as Adderall, Vyvanse, or Ritalin?

Um… I’m not sure. Like, I know the names because people talk about them, and I’ve heard classmates mention them around exams and stuff, but I don’t think I’m currently taking one of those.

I’d have to check the exact names of anything if that matters, because I’m bad at remembering medication names, but no, I don’t think I’m on Adderall or Vyvanse or Ritalin right now.
Does this urge to move happen even when you’re relaxing, like watching TV or hanging out at home?

Yeah… it does. Like even if I’m “relaxing,” I don’t really relax the way other people seem to. If I’m watching TV at home, I’ll be shifting around, getting up for no real reason, pacing during parts I’m not even bored by.

It’s kind of the same feeling as in the classroom or in the radiology suite, where I’m supposed to just sit still or stand in one place and focus, and I feel like I’m crawling out of my skin. I tried to just tough it out for months, because I figured maybe I just needed to get used to it, but I still end up moving around or finding some excuse to go do something.
As a child, were you also restless at home?

Yeah, I think so. My parents still bring it up, actually—not like every day, but if school comes up they’ll mention those elementary school conferences where the teachers were saying I was always out of my seat, calling things out, or already starting before the directions were even finished.

And that was way before middle school. Like, not just something that started with radiology training or college stuff. I guess at home I was kind of the same way too, but the teacher conference stories are what my parents always remember.

Tasks… I don’t know, daily life stuff kind of piles up. But I don’t want to make it sound dramatic. I just feel like I’m always trying to keep a mental list, and then something else happens and the list disappears. Sorry, I’m rambling. So… yes, I guess I do have some trouble with that.

patient.answer:
Um… yeah, I’m not totally sure how to answer that. I mean, I definitely don’t jump excitedly into stuff like paperwork or reading something long, but I don’t know if I “often put it off” in the way you mean.

Like, if I have to read something for class, I’ll tell myself I’m going to start after I get water or check one thing, and then somehow I’m reorganizing my desk or watching some random video about, like, how airport scanners work—which is kind of related to radiology, I guess, but not actually the assignment.

Sorry, I’m getting off track. So… I guess I do put off that kind of stuff sometimes, especially if it feels like it’s going to take a lot of sitting still and focusing, but I haven’t really kept track of how much.

So… I haven’t really noticed feeling physically tense all the time, no.

doctor.intent: Differentiate lifelong ADHD-related hyperactivity from akathisia or anxiety by confirming whether the same restlessness is present across settings in adulthood, not just in stressful situations.
doctor.question: Does this urge to move happen even when you’re relaxing, like watching TV or hanging out at home?

target_item.name: Feeling_Restless
target_item.manifestation: I came in because I feel like I’m crawling out of my skin whenever I’m supposed to sit still in the radiology suite or classroom, and after months of trying to tough it out I still end up pacing, shifting, or finding some excuse to move.
target_item.reason: The question is directly about feeling an urge to move or restlessness even during situations where the patient would normally be sitting still or relaxing.

patient.answer:
Yeah… it does. Like even if I’m “relaxing,” I don’t really relax the way other people seem to. If I’m watching TV at home, I’ll be shifting around, getting up for no real reason, pacing during parts I’m not even bored by.

It’s kind of the same feeling as in the classroom or in the radiology suite, where I’m supposed to just sit still or stand in one place and focus, and I feel like I’m crawling out of my skin. I tried to just tough it out for months, because I figured maybe I just needed to get used to it, but I still end up moving around or finding some excuse to go do something.

Yeah, I think so. My parents still bring it up, actually—not like every day, but if school comes up they’ll mention those elementary school conferences where the teachers were saying I was always out of my seat, calling things out, or already starting before the directions were even finished.

And that was way before middle school. Like, not just something that started with radiology training or college stuff. I guess at home I was kind of the same way too, but the teacher conference stories are what my parents always remember.
